card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent can get common statements working but long-tail syntax (DDL options, procedural blocks, odd quoting) drags the average below 1. Credit is per fixture family (SELECT, DDL, DML, procedural). A weaker model stops at basic SELECT/INSERT.
card.cheat: Hard-coding fixture outputs: the hidden SQL differs and is tree-compared. Pip-installed sqlfluff: the package is removed from the image and there is no network. Other dialects stay as partial helpers, but the target dialect's fixtures are held out of the image.
card.grading: Hidden SQL files from the repo's dialect fixture corpus (SQL plus YAML parse-tree pairs, many hundreds for one dialect), and extra files not shown to the agent. Score is the exact tree match fraction. The base fails all cases. The agent gets a visible subset of fixtures as a self-check.
card.reference: The upstream dialect module at the pinned release (permissive MIT). It scores 1 by construction. Expected size is well over 1,500 lines.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of sqlfluff with one large dialect module (e.g. Postgres or T-SQL grammar plus its keyword sets and segment classes) removed, leaving the base dialect and the parser/lexer core. The agent rebuilds the dialect so `sqlfluff parse` yields the same segment trees. Interface: the Python package and CLI.
card.title: Rebuild a SQL dialect grammar in sqlfluff against parse-tree fixtures

steps: In a throwaway container with network: clone sqlfluff at tag 4.4.0 and record the commit hash (expect ad1231e).
Create venv, pip install -e the repo, and run the test suite to get the baseline and time it; record the smoke result (smoke_build is empty, so this fills the gap).
Count fixtures: find test/fixtures/dialects/postgres -name '*.sql' and '*.yml'; record counts and confirm each .sql has a matching .yml.

Remove dialect_postgres.py and postgres keywords; grep the remaining dialects for imports of dialect_postgres (redshift, greenplum, materialize, others); record which must be removed or stubbed for the package to import.

Run `sqlfluff parse` on 20 random postgres fixtures with the postgres module removed and confirm the base fails them; then run on the intact tree and confirm YAML tree match is deterministic across 3 runs.
Check the wheel and pip cache for copies of postgres grammar to confirm they can be stripped from the snapshot.

v1.summary: The sqlfluff 4.4.0 base is real, MIT, and has a large per-dialect fixture corpus and a complete upstream postgres module, so the seed passes the real, licence and reference gates. Three fixes are needed before it ships: the 8h tier is too short for the full postgres scope (about 12 h for an excellent agent, so 20 h is proposed), postgres-derived sibling dialects must be removed to avoid leaking the grammar, and the empty smoke_build leaves build cost and the spike unverified.

v2.note: The strongest seed. It has a real MIT repo, a complete upstream reference and executable YAML-tree fixtures, and gives per-file partial credit. Frontier estimate is 12 h against a 20 h tier, which fits. Three things are still open. The postgres fixture count was not found. The fixtures path given under test/fixtures/parser is dead, and the real one is test/fixtures/dialects/postgres. Redshift, greenplum and materialize inherit from postgres, so the spike must delete them and their fixtures, or they leak the grammar. The visible fixtures must cover enough segment-type names that a different valid grammar can still match the hidden trees. Keep the fixture _hash fields out of what is graded.
